payload.body: The chroma filterbank is a fixed 12×N transformation matrix that folds a frequency spectrum into 12 pitch-class bins. Its parameters are: (1) N, the number of frequency bins in the input spectrum (matching the FFT size), (2) the 12 pitch-class center frequencies (typically derived from the equal-tempered scale at 440 Hz reference), and (3) the window function applied to each bin (commonly Gaussian or triangular). The persistence mechanism is the fixed mathematical mapping: for each frame, the filterbank multiplies the spectral vector by the 12×N matrix, summing energy at all frequencies that harmonically correspond to each of the 12 pitch classes (C through B). This produces the octave-invariant chroma vector. The filterbank itself — distinct from the chroma vector it produces — is the transformation kernel, stored as a fixed weight matrix in MIR toolkits (Librosa, Essentia).
